title: N. Notation and Symbols — Detailed Reference
description: An organized symbol glossary for the multi-sheeted n-gon tiling project. Symbols are grouped by role (algebra, geometry, group/bundle, spectrum, dimension, family). Each entry gives the symbol's meaning, typical use, and pointer to the relevant section of the main glossary.

rational-numbers.summary: The field of rational numbers, of characteristic 0.
rational-numbers.definition: The field $\mathbb{Q}$ of rational numbers, having characteristic 0.

real-numbers.summary: The field of real numbers, the metric completion of $\mathbb{Q}$.
real-numbers.definition: The field $\mathbb{R}$ of real numbers, obtained as the metric completion of $\mathbb{Q}$.

complex-numbers.definition: The field $\mathbb{C}$ of complex numbers, which is the algebraic closure of $\mathbb{R}$.

quadratic-field.summary: A degree-2 extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ generated by $\sqrt{d}$.
quadratic-field.definition: The quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$, a degree-2 extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ for a square-free integer $d$.

real-quadratic-field-sqrt5.summary: The real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ with discriminant 5; the project's main field.
real-quadratic-field-sqrt5.definition: The real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$, having discriminant 5. This is the primary algebraic field for the multi-sheeted pentagon tiling project, containing the golden ratio $\phi = (1+\sqrt{5})/2$.

ring-of-integers-phi.summary: The ring of integers $\mathbb{Z}[\phi]$ of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$; a PID and UFD with elements $a + b\phi$.
ring-of-integers-phi.definition: The ring of integers $\mathbb{Z}[\phi]$ of the field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$. It is a principal ideal domain (PID) and unique factorization domain (UFD). Elements take the form $a + b\phi$ for $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$.

formulas.description: Field norm of an element $a + b\phi$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\phi]$.

variables.a: Integer coefficient of the rational part

gaussian-integers.summary: The ring $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ of Gaussian integers with norm $a^2 + b^2$; used in pinwheel constructions.
gaussian-integers.definition: The ring $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ of Gaussian integers, consisting of complex numbers $a + bi$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$. The norm is $N(a+bi) = a^2 + b^2$. Used in pinwheel tiling constructions.

cyclotomic-field.summary: The field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ generated by a primitive $n$-th root of unity.
cyclotomic-field.definition: The cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$, generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $n$-th root of unity $\zeta_n = e^{2\pi i/n}$.

golden-ratio.summary: The golden ratio $\phi = (1+\sqrt{5})/2 \approx 1.618$; the fundamental unit of $\mathbb{Z}[\phi]$.
golden-ratio.definition: The golden ratio $\phi = (1 + \sqrt{5})/2 \approx 1.618$. It is the fundamental unit of the ring $\mathbb{Z}[\phi]$ and appears throughout pentagonal and icosahedral geometry.

galois-conjugate-psi.summary: The Galois conjugate $\psi = (1-\sqrt{5})/2 \approx -0.618 = -1/\phi$ of the golden ratio. Also overloaded as wave function in physics context.
galois-conjugate-psi.definition: The Galois conjugate of $\phi$, defined as $\psi = (1 - \sqrt{5})/2 \approx -0.618 = -1/\phi$. Note: $\psi$ is also overloaded as the wave function symbol in physics contexts; disambiguation is by context.

formulas.description: Definition of the Galois conjugate of $\phi$.

primitive-root-of-unity.summary: The primitive $n$-th root of unity $\zeta_n = e^{2\pi i/n}$.
primitive-root-of-unity.definition: The primitive $n$-th root of unity $\zeta_n = e^{2\pi i / n}$, a generator of the cyclic group of $n$-th roots of unity in $\mathbb{C}$.

formulas.description: Definition of the primitive $n$-th root of unity.

field-norm.summary: The multiplicative field norm $N(\cdot)$; for $\mathbb{Z}[\phi]$: $N(a+b\phi) = a^2 + ab - b^2$.
field-norm.definition: The field norm $N(\cdot)$, a multiplicative map satisfying $N(xy) = N(x)N(y)$. For elements of $\mathbb{Z}[\phi]$: $N(a + b\phi) = a^2 + ab - b^2$.

galois-automorphism.summary: The Galois automorphism $\sigma$ with $\sigma(\sqrt{d}) = -\sqrt{d}$. Also overloaded as CA cell state or spin variable.
galois-automorphism.definition: The Galois automorphism $\sigma$ of a quadratic field, defined by $\sigma(\sqrt{d}) = -\sqrt{d}$. Note: $\sigma$ is also overloaded as a CA cell state or general spin variable; context disambiguates.

formulas.description: Action of the Galois automorphism on the generator of a quadratic field.

variables.d: Square-free integer defining the quadratic field

galois-group.summary: The Galois group $\text{Gal}(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{Q})$ of automorphisms of $\mathbb{F}$ fixing $\mathbb{Q}$.
galois-group.definition: The Galois group $\text{Gal}(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{Q})$, consisting of all field automorphisms of $\mathbb{F}$ that fix $\mathbb{Q}$ pointwise.

fibonacci-number.summary: The Fibonacci numbers $F_n$ defined by $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ with $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$.
fibonacci-number.definition: The Fibonacci sequence $\{F_n\}$ defined by the recurrence $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ with initial conditions $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$.

lucas-number.summary: The Lucas numbers $L_n$, companion to Fibonacci; $L_{n+1} = L_n + L_{n-1}$, $L_0 = 2$, $L_1 = 1$.
lucas-number.definition: The Lucas sequence $\{L_n\}$, the companion sequence to Fibonacci, defined by $L_{n+1} = L_n + L_{n-1}$ with initial conditions $L_0 = 2$, $L_1 = 1$.

interior-angle.summary: The interior angle $\theta$ of a polygon at a vertex; for a regular pentagon $\theta = 108°$.
interior-angle.definition: The interior angle $\theta$ of a polygon at a vertex. For a regular pentagon, $\theta = 108°$.

examples.title: Pentagon
examples.body: A regular pentagon has interior angle $\theta = 108°$ at each vertex.

angular-deficit.summary: The angular deficit $\delta = 2\pi - \sum\theta$ around a vertex; for a pentagon vertex $\delta = 36°$.
angular-deficit.definition: The angular deficit $\delta$ at a vertex, defined as $\delta = 2\pi - \sum \theta$ where the sum is over all polygon angles meeting at that vertex. For a regular pentagon vertex, $\delta = 36°$.

examples.title: Pentagon vertex
examples.body: At a vertex where three pentagons meet: $\delta = 360° - 3 \times 108° = 36°$.

variables.\\theta_i: Interior angle of the $i$-th polygon meeting at the vertex

dihedral-angle.summary: The dihedral angle $\alpha$ of a polyhedron along an edge; the 3D analogue of the interior angle.
dihedral-angle.definition: The dihedral angle $\alpha$ of a polyhedron along an edge, measuring the angle between two adjacent faces. This is the 3D analogue of the interior angle $\theta$. Note: $\alpha$ is also overloaded as a generic algebraic number or coupling constant.

polygon-polyhedron.summary: Capital $P$ for a generic polytope; $P_0$ for the seed tile of an expansion family.
polygon-polyhedron.definition: Capital $P$ denotes a generic polygon or polyhedron (polytope). $P_0$ specifically denotes the seed tile from which an expansion family is generated.

projected-vertex-set.summary: The projected vertex set $\mathcal{L}$; image of multi-sheeted vertices in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
projected-vertex-set.definition: The projected vertex set $\mathcal{L}$, defined as the image of multi-sheeted vertices under the projection map $\pi: \mathcal{M} \to \mathbb{R}^n$.

covering-space.definition: The covering space $\mathcal{M}$, a multi-sheeted manifold lying above the base space $\mathbb{R}^n$. The projection $\pi: \mathcal{M} \to \mathbb{R}^n$ maps each sheet to the base.

projection-map.summary: The projection $\pi: \mathcal{M} \to \mathbb{R}^n$ from sheet to base. Also overloaded as the ratio of circle circumference to diameter, and as $\pi_1$ for the fundamental group.
projection-map.definition: The projection map $\pi: \mathcal{M} \to \mathbb{R}^n$ sending each point on a sheet to its image in the base space. Note: $\pi$ is overloaded — it also denotes the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, and appears as $\pi_1$ for the fundamental group.

euler-characteristic.summary: The Euler characteristic $\chi = v - e + f$ for polyhedra.
euler-characteristic.definition: The Euler characteristic $\chi = v - e + f$, a topological invariant of a polyhedron (or more generally a CW-complex), where $v$ is the number of vertices, $e$ the number of edges, and $f$ the number of faces.

examples.title: Sphere
examples.body: For any convex polyhedron (topologically a sphere): $\chi = 2$.

edge-set.summary: The edge set $E = E_A \cup E_I$ partitioned into active and inactive subsets.
edge-set.definition: The edge set $E$ of a tiling graph, partitioned as $E = E_A \cup E_I$ where $E_A$ is the active edge set (generators come from these) and $E_I$ is the inactive edge set (decorative or weak-gauge).

face-set.summary: The face set $F$ of a 3D polyhedron; the 3D analogue of the edge set.
face-set.definition: The face set $F$ of a 3D polyhedron, analogous to the edge set $E$ in 2D.

vertex-set.summary: The vertex set $V$ of a polygon, polyhedron, or graph.
vertex-set.definition: The vertex set $V$ of a polygon, polyhedron, or graph. Standard notation.

vortex-set.summary: The vortex set $\Sigma$; the set of vortex vertices in $\mathbb{R}^n$ around which sheets wind.
vortex-set.definition: The vortex set $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, consisting of the vortex vertices around which the multi-sheeted structure winds. The punctured space $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus \Sigma$ forms the base of the multi-sheeted bundle.

punctured-space.summary: The punctured space $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus \Sigma$; the base of the multi-sheeted bundle.
punctured-space.definition: The punctured space $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus \Sigma$, obtained by removing the vortex set $\Sigma$ from $\mathbb{R}^n$. This serves as the base space of the multi-sheeted bundle.

orientation-group.summary: The orientation group $\Gamma$; a subgroup of $O(n)$ generated by rotational parts of the expansion generators.
orientation-group.definition: The orientation group $\Gamma$, a subgroup of the orthogonal group $O(n)$ generated by the rotational parts of the expansion family generators.

fiber-group.summary: The fiber group $G$ indexing the sheets; e.g., $\mathbb{Z}_{10}$ for the pentagon.
fiber-group.definition: The fiber group $G$, which indexes the sheets of the multi-sheeted covering. For the pentagon, $G = \mathbb{Z}_{10}$.

examples.title: Pentagon
examples.body: For the regular pentagon tiling, the fiber group is $G = \mathbb{Z}_{10}$, reflecting the 10-fold sheet structure.

orthogonal-group.summary: The orthogonal group $O(n)$ of distance-preserving linear maps of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
orthogonal-group.definition: The orthogonal group $O(n)$, consisting of all distance-preserving (isometric) linear maps of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Note: $O$ is overloaded with the octahedral group $O$; distinguished by the argument $n$.

special-orthogonal-group.summary: The special orthogonal group $SO(n)$; the orientation-preserving subgroup of $O(n)$.
special-orthogonal-group.definition: The special orthogonal group $SO(n)$, the subgroup of $O(n)$ consisting of orientation-preserving (determinant $+1$) isometries of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

spin-group.summary: The spin group $\text{Spin}(n)$; the double cover of $SO(n)$.
spin-group.definition: The spin group $\text{Spin}(n)$, which is the universal double cover of the special orthogonal group $SO(n)$.

special-unitary-group-su2.definition: The special unitary group $SU(2)$, isomorphic to $\text{Spin}(3)$, which is the double cover of $SO(3)$.

icosahedral-group.summary: The icosahedral group $I \cong A_5$ of order 60.
icosahedral-group.definition: The icosahedral group $I$, isomorphic to the alternating group $A_5$, of order 60. It is the rotation symmetry group of the icosahedron and dodecahedron.

binary-icosahedral-group.summary: The binary icosahedral group $2I$ of order 120; the double cover of $I$ in $SU(2)$.
binary-icosahedral-group.definition: The binary icosahedral group $2I$, of order 120, which is the preimage of the icosahedral group $I$ under the double cover $SU(2) \to SO(3)$.

octahedral-group.summary: The octahedral group $O \cong S_4$ of order 24. Overloaded with $O(n)$; read by context.
octahedral-group.definition: The octahedral group $O$, isomorphic to the symmetric group $S_4$, of order 24. It is the rotation symmetry group of the octahedron and cube. Note: $O$ is overloaded with the orthogonal group $O(n)$; distinguished by context.

tetrahedral-group.summary: The tetrahedral group $T \cong A_4$ of order 12.
tetrahedral-group.definition: The tetrahedral group $T$, isomorphic to the alternating group $A_4$, of order 12. It is the rotation symmetry group of the tetrahedron.

dihedral-group.summary: The dihedral group $D_n$; symmetry group of the regular $n$-gon, of order $2n$.
dihedral-group.definition: The dihedral group $D_n$, the symmetry group of the regular $n$-gon, of order $2n$. It is generated by a rotation of order $n$ and a reflection.

cyclic-group.definition: The cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_n$ of order $n$, the unique (up to isomorphism) group with $n$ elements generated by a single element of order $n$.

symmetric-group.summary: The symmetric group $S_n$ of all permutations of $n$ elements.
symmetric-group.definition: The symmetric group $S_n$, consisting of all permutations of $n$ elements, of order $n!$.

alternating-group.summary: The alternating group $A_n$ of even permutations of $n$ elements.
alternating-group.definition: The alternating group $A_n$, consisting of all even permutations of $n$ elements, of order $n!/2$.

affine-group.summary: The affine group $\text{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of affine maps of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
affine-group.definition: The affine group $\text{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, consisting of all invertible affine maps of $\mathbb{R}^n$ (linear part plus translation).

fundamental-group.summary: The fundamental group $\pi_1$; homotopy classes of loops based at a point.
fundamental-group.definition: The fundamental group $\pi_1(X, x_0)$ of a topological space $X$ at basepoint $x_0$, consisting of homotopy classes of loops based at $x_0$.

sheet-transition.summary: The sheet transition map $\tau: E \to G$ labeling edges with fiber-group elements.
sheet-transition.definition: The sheet transition map $\tau: E \to G$, which assigns to each edge $e \in E$ an element of the fiber group $G$, encoding how the sheet index changes when crossing that edge.

generator.summary: The $k$-th generator $g_k$ of the expansion family, with linear part $A_k$ and translation $\mathbf{b}_k$.
generator.definition: The $k$-th generator $g_k$ of the expansion family, an affine map of the form $g_k(x) = A_k x + \mathbf{b}_k$, where $A_k$ is the linear (rotational/scaling) part and $\mathbf{b}_k$ is the translation vector.

formulas.description: Affine form of the $k$-th expansion generator.

adjacency-graph.summary: The adjacency graph $\mathcal{G}$; one vertex per tile, edges from generators.
adjacency-graph.definition: The adjacency graph $\mathcal{G}$ of the tiling, with one vertex per tile and edges connecting tiles related by the expansion generators.

adjacency-matrix.summary: The adjacency matrix $A$ with $A_{ij} = 1$ if $i \sim j$.
adjacency-matrix.definition: The adjacency matrix $A$ of a graph, where $A_{ij} = 1$ if vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent (connected by an edge), and $A_{ij} = 0$ otherwise.

degree-matrix.summary: The degree matrix $D$; diagonal matrix of vertex degrees.
degree-matrix.definition: The degree matrix $D$, a diagonal matrix where $D_{ii}$ equals the degree (number of neighbors) of vertex $i$.

graph-laplacian.summary: The graph Laplacian $\Delta = D - A$. Overloaded with angular deficit $\delta$; typeset distinguishes.
graph-laplacian.definition: The graph Laplacian $\Delta = D - A$, where $D$ is the degree matrix and $A$ is the adjacency matrix. Its eigenvalues encode spectral properties of the graph. Note: $\Delta$ is overloaded with the angular deficit; typically $\Delta$ for the Laplacian and $\delta$ for the deficit.

density-of-states.summary: The density of states $\rho(\lambda)$; histogram of Laplacian eigenvalues.
density-of-states.definition: The density of states $\rho(\lambda)$, the normalized histogram (spectral measure) of eigenvalues of the graph Laplacian.

spectral-gap.summary: The spectral gap $\lambda_1$; the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the graph Laplacian.
spectral-gap.definition: The spectral gap $\lambda_1$, defined as the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the graph Laplacian $\Delta$. It controls the mixing time of random walks and connectivity properties.

chebyshev-polynomial.summary: The Chebyshev polynomial $T_k$ of degree $k$; basis for the Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM).
chebyshev-polynomial.definition: The Chebyshev polynomial $T_k$ of degree $k$, used as the basis for the Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM) for computing spectral properties.

chebyshev-moment.definition: The $k$-th Chebyshev moment $\mu_k = \frac{1}{n} \text{Tr}(T_k(\hat{H}))$, used in the Kernel Polynomial Method to reconstruct the density of states.

return-probability.summary: The return probability $P_0(t)$; probability that a random walk returns to its origin at time $t$.
return-probability.definition: The return probability $P_0(t)$, the probability that a random walk starting at the origin returns to the origin after $t$ steps.

mean-squared-displacement.summary: The mean-squared displacement $\langle \Delta x^2 \rangle(t)$; a random walk metric.
mean-squared-displacement.definition: The mean-squared displacement $\langle \Delta x^2 \rangle(t)$, measuring the average squared distance traveled by a random walk after $t$ steps.

formulas.description: Scaling of mean-squared displacement with walk dimension $d_w$.

bfs-volume.summary: The BFS volume $V(r)$; number of tiles within graph distance $r$ from the origin.
bfs-volume.definition: The BFS (breadth-first search) volume $V(r)$, defined as the number of tiles within graph distance $r$ from a fixed origin tile.

formulas.description: Volume growth law defining the effective dimension.

loop-closure-count.summary: The loop closure count $k_{\text{close}}$; number of tiles needed to close a fundamental loop.
loop-closure-count.definition: The loop closure count $k_{\text{close}}$, the number of tiles required to close a fundamental loop in the adjacency graph.

effective-dimension.summary: The effective dimension $d_{\text{eff}}$ from volume scaling $V(r) \sim r^{d_{\text{eff}}}$.
effective-dimension.definition: The effective (connectivity) dimension $d_{\text{eff}}$, extracted from the volume growth law $V(r) \sim r^{d_{\text{eff}}}$ of the BFS ball.

formulas.description: Volume growth law defining the effective dimension.

spectral-dimension.definition: The spectral dimension $d_{\text{spec}}$, extracted from the low-energy behavior of the density of states: $\rho(\lambda) \sim \lambda^{d_{\text{spec}}/2 - 1}$.

formulas.description: Low-energy density of states scaling defining the spectral dimension.

walk-dimension.summary: The walk dimension $d_w$ from $\langle \Delta x^2 \rangle \sim t^{2/d_w}$.
walk-dimension.definition: The walk dimension $d_w$, extracted from the anomalous diffusion scaling $\langle \Delta x^2 \rangle \sim t^{2/d_w}$.

formulas.description: Anomalous diffusion scaling defining the walk dimension.

hausdorff-dimension.summary: The Hausdorff dimension $d_H$; the measure-theoretic dimension.
hausdorff-dimension.definition: The Hausdorff dimension $d_H$, a measure-theoretic notion of dimension that can take non-integer values for fractal sets.

box-counting-dimension.summary: The box-counting dimension $d_B$; equals $d_H$ for self-similar fractals.
box-counting-dimension.definition: The box-counting dimension $d_B$, computed by covering a set with boxes of size $\epsilon$ and counting how many are needed. For self-similar fractals, $d_B = d_H$.

alexander-orbach-relation.summary: The Alexander–Orbach relation $d_{\text{spec}} = 2 d_{\text{eff}} / d_w$ linking spectral, effective, and walk dimensions.
alexander-orbach-relation.definition: The Alexander–Orbach relation $d_{\text{spec}} = 2 d_{\text{eff}} / d_w$, which relates the spectral dimension, effective (connectivity) dimension, and walk dimension of a fractal or disordered medium.

expansion-family.summary: The expansion family $\mathcal{F}$; all tile copies generated from the seed $P_0$. $\mathcal{F}_A$ is the restricted family using only active edges.
expansion-family.definition: The expansion family $\mathcal{F}$, consisting of all tile copies generated from the seed tile $P_0$ by repeated application of the generators. The restricted expansion family $\mathcal{F}_A$ is generated using only the active edge subset $E_A$.

active-edge-set.summary: The active edge set $E_A$; edges from which generators are derived.
active-edge-set.definition: The active edge set $E_A \subseteq E$, consisting of edges (or faces in 3D) from which the expansion generators are derived.

inactive-edge-set.summary: The inactive edge set $E_I$; decorative or weak-gauge edges.
inactive-edge-set.definition: The inactive edge set $E_I \subseteq E$, consisting of edges (or faces in 3D) that are decorative or weak-gauge and do not contribute to the expansion generators.

algebraic-field.summary: A generic algebraic field $\mathbb{F}$; the field of vertex coordinates.
algebraic-field.definition: A generic algebraic field $\mathbb{F}$, used to denote the field in which vertex coordinates of the tiling live (e.g., $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$).

integer-hypercubic-lattice.definition: The standard integer hypercubic lattice $\mathbb{Z}^n$, the target lattice for coordinate representations.

pentagonal-lattice.summary: The pentagonal lattice $\mathbb{Z}[\phi]^n$; vertices of the pentagonal expansion.
pentagonal-lattice.definition: The pentagonal lattice $\mathbb{Z}[\phi]^n$, consisting of $n$-tuples of elements from $\mathbb{Z}[\phi]$. These are the vertex coordinates of the pentagonal expansion tiling.

wave-function.summary: The wave function $\psi$ in quantum mechanics. Overloaded with the Galois conjugate of $\phi$; context disambiguates.
wave-function.definition: The wave function $\psi$ in quantum mechanics. Note: $\psi$ is overloaded with the Galois conjugate of $\phi$ in algebra; context disambiguates.

gauge-field.summary: The gauge field $A_\mu$; a continuum gauge connection.
gauge-field.definition: The gauge field $A_\mu$, a continuum gauge connection (1-form) whose curvature is the field strength $F_{\mu\nu}$.

field-strength.summary: The field strength $F_{\mu\nu}$; the curvature of the gauge field $A_\mu$.
field-strength.definition: The field strength tensor $F_{\mu\nu}$, the curvature of the gauge connection $A_\mu$.

reduced-planck-constant.definition: The reduced Planck constant $\hbar = h / (2\pi)$, the fundamental quantum of action.

bf-theory-fields.summary: The BF theory fields $B$ (Lagrange multiplier) and $F$ (curvature).
bf-theory-fields.definition: The fields of BF theory: $B$ is a Lagrange multiplier form and $F$ is the curvature (field strength) of a gauge connection. BF theory is a topological field theory.

magnetic-flux.summary: The magnetic flux $\Phi$ in the Aharonov–Bohm context.
magnetic-flux.definition: The magnetic flux $\Phi$, appearing in the Aharonov–Bohm effect where a charged particle acquires a phase proportional to the enclosed magnetic flux.

big-o.definition: Big-O notation $O(f)$: $g = O(f)$ means there exist constants $C > 0$ and $x_0$ such that $|g(x)| \leq C|f(x)|$ for all $x > x_0$.

big-omega.definition: Big-Omega notation $\Omega(f)$: $g = \Omega(f)$ means there exist constants $C > 0$ and $x_0$ such that $|g(x)| \geq C|f(x)|$ for all $x > x_0$.

big-theta.summary: Big-Theta notation $\Theta(f)$; tight asymptotic bound. Equivalent to $f \asymp g$ (same order).
big-theta.definition: Big-Theta notation $\Theta(f)$: $g = \Theta(f)$ means $g = O(f)$ and $g = \Omega(f)$. Equivalently written $f \asymp g$ (same order).

little-o.summary: Little-o notation $o(f)$; strict asymptotic upper bound.

asymptotic-equivalence.definition: Asymptotic equivalence $f \sim g$: $f(x)/g(x) \to 1$ as $x \to \infty$. Note: $\sim$ is also overloaded for adjacency and general equivalence relations.

same-order.definition: Same-order notation $f \asymp g$, meaning $f = \Theta(g)$: both $f = O(g)$ and $g = O(f)$.
